pr_title: subsys: lorawan: add devicetime request support
pr_body:
Add devicetime request support:
-> Function to request devicetime : optionnally force sending message/optionnally blocking call
-> Function to retrieve current time from loramac-node stack
Fixes #55072
pr_comments: @Mani-Sadhasivam  @JordanYates please take a look, thanks!
How does this relate to the LoRaWAN clock synchronisation added in #51328?
@JordanYates This PR is related to MAC DeviceTime commands (DeviceTimeReq, DeviceTimeAns) supported in LoRaWAN 1.0.3.

Updated according to comments

Updated according to comments.
Split in two commits for callback signature update and the second for device time request feature.

Requested changes applied.
Currently, as  _lorawan_get_time_ could return an inconsistent time (begins from epoch 0) and requires user to check if date is valid, a better approach could be based on _lorawan_clock_sync_get(uint32_t *gps_time)_

- Step 1

1. Declare static boolean variable in lorawan.c
2. On DevTimeAnswer received, toggle boolean value to true
3. _lorawan_get_time_ returns -EAGAIN while DevTime has been updated

The new prototype would be:
```
/**
 * @brief Retrieve the current time from LoRaWAN stack
 *
 * The epoch started on 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.
 *
 * @param epoch_time Synchronized time in epoch format truncated to 32-bit.
 *
 * @return 0 if successful, -EAGAIN if the time is not yet updated.
 */
int lorawan_get_time(uint32_t *epoch_time);
```

This avoid user to check time validity

- Step 2

If you are ok with that I could factorize
(bool lorawan_adr_enable
bool time_updated_once) into an atomic flags
Your proposed changes make sense to me. I think it just needs to be clear the difference between `lorawan_get_time` and `lorawan_clock_sync_get`

@JordanYates Please let me know if you think I should add more information about devtimereq (lorawan_request_device_time) as details doxygen part and maybe add apptimereq (lorawan_clock_sync_get) informations in the same way

> @martinjaeger I switched to atomic to treat boolean ADR and boolean time updated at least once into a single variable. I can revert it if you prefer.

Keep the single flags variable instead of multiple `bool` please. As mentioned previously, either option is an API change, but the flags lets us continue to extend the options without further breaks.

> Beside, I can switch to GPS epoch time if you prefer too : let me test it again on a gateway on next Wednesday.

Please do this, it is preferable over a Unix time which we know is significantly wrong.
If possible, try and return the subseconds portion as well, I suspect it will be useful for class B as well as enabling generally better time synchronisation.
I agree with @JordanYates. The flags are fine and I understand the reason behind them now. Also agree to use GPS epoch and leave conversion to proper unix timestamp to the user.
You are right with leap seconds. When LoRaWAN DevTimeAnswer gives 2023-10-24T10:06:14, the current (real) time is 2023-10-24T10:05:58 (with human reading tolerance :))
@martinjaeger @JordanYates GPS based time is missing at this time but I would test it before pushing something
@RomainPelletant do you have any updates? I'd be happy to support with testing.

issue_context.title: subsys: lorawan: DeviceTime request
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
LoRaWAN 1.0.3 specifications includes DeviceTime request as MAC commands to get current time from gateway

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A function to request DeviceTimeReq (with optionnaly force sending empty message - piggy-back, and optionnally blocking function call until DeviceTimeAns received)
A function to get current time from loramac-node stack

review_comments:
I suggest to mention clearly that this is UNIX epoch and not GPS epoch (which is used in AppClockSync):

```suggestion
/**
 * @brief Retrieve the current UNIX timestamp from LoRaWAN stack updated by
 * DeviceTimeAns on MAC layer.
 *
 * The UNIX epoch starts at 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.
 *
 * @param unix_time Synchronized time in seconds truncated to 32-bit.
 *
 * @return 0 if successful, -EAGAIN if the time is not yet updated.
 */
int lorawan_device_time_get(uint32_t *unix_time);
```

Are you sure about that? As shown in an earlier screenshot, section 5.9 of the spec says:

> (*) The GPS epoch (i.e., January 6, 1980 00:00:00 UTC) is used as origin. The seconds field is the number of seconds elapsed since the origin. This field increases monotonically by 1 every second. To convert this field to UTC time, the leap seconds SHALL be taken into account

The timestamp is transferred in GPS epoch format, but this function gets the time through [SysTimeGet](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/loramac-node/blob/842413c5fb98707eb5f26e619e8e792453877897/src/system/systime.h#L122), which uses the UNIX epoch.

See here for the code section doing the conversion: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/loramac-node/blob/842413c5fb98707eb5f26e619e8e792453877897/src/mac/LoRaMac.c#L2552-L2578

However, it looks like it is ignoring the leap seconds...

Great, so the time is only out by 20 something seconds. I would advocate for translating the value back to GPS time in our function then. Let the user perform conversions starting from a correct time, together with any knowledge of leap seconds they may have.

The problem is that the received timestamp is processed in LoRaMac.c already and we don't see the raw data in the Zephyr application, in contrast to app clock sync.

While the 20 seconds don't seem a lot for many applications, they will have to be compensated to be useful for Class B.

@RomainPelletant have you tested your code and checked how accurate the received time is?

Now that Zephyr has a RTC API we could use both DeviceTimeReq and AppClockSync to set the time of the RTC instead of coming up with custom clock/time APIs based on uncommon epochs. Thoughts?

> The problem is that the received timestamp is processed in LoRaMac.c already and we don't see the raw data in the Zephyr application, in contrast to app clock sync.

Sure, but we know the hardcoded offset they use and can reverse it in our function.

> Now that Zephyr has a RTC API we could use both DeviceTimeReq and AppClockSync to set the time of the RTC instead of coming up with custom clock/time APIs based on uncommon epochs. Thoughts?

Not really a fan, are we adding `gmtime` into our libraries now? It makes more sense to me to leave it to the user to perform some action. Even using the RTC API would require providing the device, so it couldn't be automatic either.
I think the content of this function can be moved directly into `lorawan_request_device_time`. It's only called once and doesn't help to make the code flow more clear.

For consistency, use `!!(...)` also here:
```suggestion
			port, !!(flags & LORAWAN_DATA_PENDING), rssi, snr,
```
